key_insight: A formally verified checker can certify a polyhedron’s vertex set using mostly combinatorial tests plus polyhedron membership checks, making proof-correct vertex certification faster than full informal enumeration.
engineering_relevance: This enables trustworthy vertex-set generation for verification and optimization workflows where both correctness and runtime matter.
method: Start from an informally computed candidate list of vertices.
Use a new completeness criterion based on an abstract simplicial complex generalizing the normal fan triangulation.
In Rocq, certify completeness or exactness with cheap combinatorial checks and membership tests to the polyhedron.
evidence_signal: Across tested polyhedra, the Rocq-to-OCaml extracted checker was typically 1.5x to over 5x faster than lrslib reverse-search vertex enumeration.
watch_item: The approach still depends on an initial candidate vertex list and on the reliability of membership tests plus the extracted checker implementation.
paper_title: Formally Certifying the Vertex Set of a Polyhedron Faster than Informal Enumeration
